preamble: Voicing and fronting of the uvular stop /q/ to the velar stop [ɡ]. It is the standard reflex of qāf in Bedouin-type Arabic (Gulf, Najdi) and the word-initial reflex of back-vowel Turkic *q in Azerbaijani.

examples.note: Historically /q/ became [ɡ]; [q] was later reintroduced in a few classicisms.
/ɡ/ is the modern reflex of earlier /q/; [q] occurs only in Standard Arabic loans such as القرآن [alqurˈʔaːn].
Azerbaijani letter q stands for [ɡ] in this word; cognate Turkish kara keeps a voiceless stop.

sources: Holes, C. (2004). Modern Arabic: Structures, Functions, and Varieties. Georgetown University Press. https://press.georgetown.edu/Book/Modern-Arabic
